description: `new <name> --path <dir> --yes` against a pre-existing *empty* (so `is_resumable_leftover`-eligible), unregistered target: real creation (`mkdir`, `git init -q -b main`, write `.gitignore`, `git add`+`commit`), real registration (`add::register` appends `[projects.freshproj]`/`[projects.freshproj.chains]` to `config.toml` and prints the `Added to ...:` block, same as a standalone `add`), then a real `start_one_by_path` attempt (new.rs:163-190). The scripted Herdr reply fails the very first call (`workspace list` exit 1) so `start_one_by_path` returns `Err` without ever reaching `pane list`/`agent list` (`FleetState::fetch`'s `call_listing(...)?` short-circuits), exercising new.rs's fallback note: `note: {name} was created and registered, but did not start: {message}` (new.rs:187-189) — distinct from the untested happy-start path, which is already covered by the `start-*` scenario family. `new`'s own exit code stays 0 either way: a start failure is reported as a note, never propagated as the command's own failure (new.rs:185-191 ends with an unconditional `Ok(())`).
